title: A short exact sequence of modules has a degreewise split short exact sequence of free resolutions
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $0\to Q\xrightarrow{u}Q'\xrightarrow{v}Q''\to0$ a short exact sequence of $R$-modules ($u$ injective, $\ker v=\operatorname{im}u$, $v$ surjective). Then there exist chain complexes of free $R$-modules $F_\bullet$, $F'_\bullet$, $F''_\bullet$ (indexed by $n\ge0$, differentials $d,d',d''$) with $R$-linear augmentations $\varepsilon:F_0\to Q$, $\varepsilon':F'_0\to Q'$, $\varepsilon'':F''_0\to Q''$ such that the three augmented complexes $\cdots\to F_1\xrightarrow{d_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}Q\to0$, $\cdots\to F'_1\to F'_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon'}Q'\to0$, $\cdots\to F''_1\to F''_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon''}Q''\to0$ are exact (free resolutions), together with morphisms of complexes $\alpha:F_\bullet\to F'_\bullet$, $\beta:F'_\bullet\to F''_\bullet$ ($d'_n\alpha_n=\alpha_{n-1}d_n$, $d''_n\beta_n=\beta_{n-1}d'_n$) satisfying $\varepsilon'\alpha_0=u\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon''\beta_0=v\varepsilon'$, and, for every $n\ge0$, $R$-linear maps $\pi_n:F'_n\to F_n$ and $s_n:F''_n\to F'_n$ (not required to commute with the differentials) with $\beta_n\alpha_n=0$, $\pi_n\alpha_n=\mathrm{id}_{F_n}$, $\beta_ns_n=\mathrm{id}_{F''_n}$ and $\alpha_n\pi_n+s_n\beta_n=\mathrm{id}_{F'_n}$. In particular $0\to F_n\xrightarrow{\alpha_n}F'_n\xrightarrow{\beta_n}F''_n\to0$ is split exact for every $n$.

proof.text: Lift Q, Q′, Q″ to the common universe max(u,v₁,v₂,v₃) with ULift.moduleEquiv and conjugate u and v. Injectivity, exactness and surjectivity are preserved by these linear equivalences. Package the resulting sequence as ResolutionSES.

For a short exact sequence E, construct P=E.A →₀ R and T=E.C →₀ R with evaluation maps η and θ, and a linear lift of θ obtained by choosing preimages of all elements of E.C under the proved surjection E.p. Define μ(x,z)=E.i(η(x))+lift(z). The endpoint evaluation maps are surjective, and an explicit subtraction and lift argument proves μ surjective. These modules and P×T are free by the Finsupp and product free-module instances.

Define ki:ker η→ker μ by x↦(x,0) and kp:ker μ→ker θ by (x,z)↦z. Injectivity of ki follows from first projection. If kp(y)=0, injectivity of E.i forces η(y.1)=0, giving exactness. For z∈ker θ, exactness of E gives a with E.i(a)=−lift(z); choose x with η(x)=a, so (x,z) lies in ker μ and maps to z. This proves kp surjective directly, without the general snake lemma.

Recursively define stage(0)=E and stage(n+1) as the short exact sequence of the three kernels just constructed. In degree n use stage(n).P, stage(n).P×stage(n).T and stage(n).T. Define differentials as the next evaluation map followed by kernel inclusion. A surjection onto ker f followed by inclusion has range ker f, and its kernel equals the kernel of the surjection because inclusion is injective. This proves all three augmented exactness assertions.

The inclusion and second projection are chain maps: for the first use the definition of μ at the next stage and the induced kernel inclusion ki; for the second use p(μ(z))=θ(z.2) at the next stage and the induced kernel projection kp. Transport the degree-zero augmentations back through ULift.moduleEquiv. Their kernels are unchanged by these injective equivalences and their surjectivity is preserved. The augmentation squares follow from μ(x,0)=i(η(x)) and p(μ(x,z))=θ(z.2). First projection and second inclusion give the remaining splitting maps. All four splitting identities are the product identities checked by extensionality. Package these explicit witnesses into the original dependent existential.
